project.name: surgidoc
project.objective: SurgiDoc: an endoscopy documentation assistant per Architecture Flowchart.png (EndoViT frame description, RAG over TigerCloud, LangGraph orchestration with generator and judge agents using Google AI Studio free models, guardrails, human approval, PDF report, Redis cache, observability). Dataset from Kaggle. Secrets in a local keys txt file. Maintain a decisions MD file consulted before decisions. Test cases for everything.

lifecycle.next_action: Review completed work and choose the next bounded outcome.

approval.reason: User approved SPEC.md (FR-1..14, NFR-1..6, AC-1..9) on 2026-10-26

assumptions.text: Voyage multimodal-3.x free allowance (200M text tokens) is from a third-party page and free trial is 3 RPM / 10K TPM without payment method; Cohere trial limits unverified. Verify before committing.
Gemini free tier may use content for product improvement; acceptable only because data is public.

invariants.text: Whenever work needs TigerCloud (or any service credential: Redis, Google AI Studio, Kaggle, Voyage, Cohere, EndoVIT endpoint), STOP and ask the user in chat to fill the matching keys.txt entries (TIGERCLOUD_SERVICE_URL, TIGERCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD, ...). Never invent values; code must raise MissingKey naming the entry.

decisions.title: Gemini-only LLMs via Google AI Studio
decisions.text: All agent LLM calls (generator, judge) use Gemini free-tier models via Google AI Studio API. No OpenRouter/GPT/Claude. Embedding: Voyage multimodal + Cohere rerank only if free tier verified at implementation time, else gemini-embedding-001.

decisions.title: Data: public only, human approval mandatory
decisions.text: Only public datasets (Kaggle newslab/cholecseg8k via kagglehub, plus public EU/Germany-focused endoscopy surgery text) are used. No real patient data. Every generated report requires human approval; output is a draft, never a diagnosis.

decisions.title: Scope: all layers, production/enterprise grade, Python
decisions.text: Build every layer in Architecture Flowchart.png (RAG, LangGraph generator/judge, guardrails, gateway, human approval, PDF, TigerCloud+Redis, observability, security/governance). Python, LangGraph, pytest, tests for every component. Secrets in git-ignored keys.txt. DECISIONS.md consulted before every decision.

decisions.title: EndoViT runs remotely, not on local CPU
decisions.text: User CPU is weak. EndoViT inference must go through a free hosted option (to be found; none confirmed). Frame-description sits behind an interface so a Gemini-vision fallback is possible.

decisions.title: MIMIC-IV-Note rejected; licence limits on KB sources
decisions.text: MIMIC-IV-Note rejected (credentialed DUA, patient notes, US ICU). ESGE KB papers are CC BY-NC(-ND) and CholecT45/CAMMA CC BY-NC-SA: non-commercial prototype only. 4 of 6 ESGE papers are Cascade guidelines for resource-limited settings, not full ESGE guidelines.

decisions.title: Embeddings: gemini-embedding-001 default, dim 768
decisions.text: Docs (ai.google.dev, 2026-10-26): gemini-embedding-2 is multimodal but aggregates a batch into ONE embedding and has no task_type, so text RAG defaults to gemini-embedding-001 (batch, taskType, we L2-normalize truncated dims). Model/dim configurable; revisit embedding-2 for frame/image search. Voyage/Cohere not used until free limits verified. Tiger Cloud: pg_textsearch BM25 (<@>) + pgvectorscale diskann + RRF k=60.

decisions.title: Vision: Gemini vision default, EndoViT optional via endpoint contract
decisions.text: EndoViT is an MAE-pretrained encoder (feature backbone), not a captioner, and no free hosted EndoViT endpoint was found. FrameDescriber interface: EndoViTClient (ENDOVIT_INFERENCE_URL/TOKEN, contract POST {image_b64,mime} -> {findings,labels}) is tried first when configured; Gemini vision (gateway role 'vision', batched frames per request to save free-tier quota) is the working default and fallback. Frame extraction via opencv-python-headless (no ffmpeg here).

decisions.title: T07 agent design: cited statements, fail-closed judge, bounded loop
decisions.text: LangGraph StateGraph retrieve->generate->(citation check)->judge->{approved|regenerate|stop}. Generator returns JSON statements each citing source ids (F<n> frame findings, K<n> KB chunks); uncited or unknown-id statements are rejected deterministically before the judge call (saves free-tier quota, enforces NFR-3). Judge (different model than generator) returns {approved, issues, feedback}; unparseable judge output = NOT approved (fail closed). Max attempts bounded (default 3); result status approved|rejected|blocked; always labelled draft. KB text and findings are wrapped as data in tags; system prompt says they are not instructions (prompt injection).

decisions.title: T09: approver self-named, fpdf2 core fonts (latin-1), Postgres tables with hypertable events
decisions.text: Approver types their own name in the name field (user is the approver); recorded as given, no authentication until T10 RBAC. Approval binds to a sha256 content hash; edits (re-checked by guardrails) reset approval; edit after approval is refused; final PDF only from an approved, hash-verified item (AC-3). PDF via fpdf2 core Helvetica: characters outside latin-1 are replaced with '?' (known ceiling, upgrade = bundle a TTF). Storage: <prefix>_reports (jsonb + bytea pdf), <prefix>_events (hypertable on at), <prefix>_rollups; parameterized SQL; prefix whitelisted.

decisions.title: T10 security design: keys.txt user registry, RBAC with separation of duties, hash-chained audit, AES-GCM primitives
decisions.text: Users live in keys.txt as SURGIDOC_USERS=Name:role+role;Name2:role (git-ignored, no new files). Roles: reviewer (view/edit/approve/reject), operator (run pipeline/view), admin (audit view/users manage/view) - admin and operator cannot approve (separation of duties). GuardedReview binds approver name to the authenticated user and audits every allow/deny; denials are audited (AC-7). Audit log: append-only, sha256 hash-chained, redacts secret-like keys, verify() + external head anchor detects truncation; Tiger Cloud sink uses advisory lock + DB triggers forbidding UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. Crypto: AES-256-GCM, versioned envelope with key fingerprint, AAD binds ciphertext to record id, optional previous key for rotation. KNOWN GAP: ReportStore (T09, closed) stores plaintext jsonb/pdf; applying encryption to stored columns needs a later task (plan reopen). No real authentication (no passwords/login) - registry is name->roles only.

decisions.title: Accepted risk: Redis without TLS (free tier)
decisions.text: User's free Redis account offers no rediss:// TLS endpoint; the project uses the plain redis:// URL (user decision 2026-10-26). Consequences: the Redis password and cached values cross the network unencrypted, so use only on trusted networks. Mitigations already in place: cache keys are SHA-256 hashes, only public-data values are cached, cache fails open. compliance check 'redis-tls' will therefore report FAIL; this is an accepted, documented exception, to be revisited if a TLS endpoint or paid plan becomes available. Do not cache anything other than public data.

decisions.title: T13: encryption at rest design, packaging guard, PDF cited sources
decisions.text: ReportStore(cipher=...): statements, sources and pdf columns are bytea AES-GCM envelopes (AAD = report id + column), explicit 'encrypted' flag per row, event details replaced by {encrypted: b64} (AAD = report id + type + revision); approver name, content hash, event type/actor/time stay plaintext for queryability and audit. Read verifies the content hash (second layer against column swapping). build_pipeline REQUIRES SURGIDOC_ENCRYPTION_KEY. PDF Sources section lists only cited sources in first-citation order; hash still covers all sources. pyproject declares runtime deps with lower bounds + extras (dev, kaggle, ocr); tests/test_packaging.py fails if any third-party import lacks a declared dependency or an optional lib is imported at module level. NOT done: clean-venv install test (WSL memory), encryption of existing rows (none exist), key rotation procedure beyond SURGIDOC_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS.

decisions.title: T17/T18 file scopes hand-edited into project.json (user-approved)
decisions.text: task set cannot change scope and task add had no scope when T17/T18 were created, so scope lists were written into .genesis/project.json by hand at the user's choice (2026-10-27); this cleared plan approval, so the plan was re-approved by the user's instruction and T17 requeued to reactivate. Use --scope on task add from now on.

decisions.title: T17: frame pictures and readable sources live inside report sources
decisions.text: Each frame source carries frame number, time t and base64 JPEG ('image'); knowledge sources carry a readable 'title' derived from the file name. They sit in the existing sources dict, so the content hash covers the picture (AC-3), ReportStore stores and encrypts them unchanged, and guardrails/judge only read 'text'. Citation labels shown to people are numbers 1,2,3 in first-citation order (pdf.citation_numbers); internal F<n>/K<n> ids never appear in the PDF. Visible report number and content hash removed from the PDF; verification unchanged. Fixed: F<n> counted usable findings only, so evidence is now carried per finding instead of by frame position. KNOWN CEILING: up to 16 frames x ~50-100 KB base64 inside the jsonb sources column (about 1-2 MB per report); move images to their own bytea column if reports get large. Title is the humanised file stem, no document metadata or page number yet.

decisions.title: T18: UI shows numbered evidence, pictures served by a token-guarded frame route
decisions.text: Status payload now exposes report.statements[{text,cites:[n]}] and report.sources[{n,kind,...}] ordered by first citation (same numbering as the PDF via pdf.citation_numbers); internal F/K ids are not displayed. Frame pictures are NOT inlined in the polled status JSON (would resend ~1 MB every 0.8 s); GET /api/frame?id=F<n> (CSRF token + Host/Origin guard, serves only bytes that start with the JPEG magic, sandbox CSP, 404 otherwise) and the page CSP gained img-src 'self'. The page still writes data with textContent only; the client re-renders only when the status changed. NOT VERIFIED IN A BROWSER: no browser exists in this environment; JS passed node --check and server routes are tested, the visual layout was not seen.

decisions.title: T18 follow-up: provenance, reviewer text editing, banner removed (user request)
decisions.text: User asked (2026-10-27): show where each source really came from, let the surgeon edit the generated text in the UI, remove the DRAFT-only banner from the UI. (1) Frame sources now say 'AI description by <Gemini vision model|EndoViT model>' (evidence carries described_by); guideline sources show title, section, document file and quote; a note under Sources says when no guideline passage supports the statements (retrieved vs cited). (2) POST /api/edit: reviewer rewords or removes statements; each kept statement keeps its original citations; revision must match (stale page refused); guardrails re-run and named rules are shown; permission report:edit (operators refused); edit refused after approval; MAX_EDIT 64 KB. The page warns and refuses to approve while edits are unsaved. (3) Banner removed from the page only; the PDF footer 'Approved by a named clinician. AI-assisted documentation; not a diagnosis.' is unchanged. Layout bug in the Sources card (stretched number badge) fixed. Not verified visually in a browser.

decisions.title: T18 follow-up 2: rejecting a draft regenerates it from the reviewer's feedback, with a toast
decisions.text: User asked (2026-10-27): after a rejection something must happen. POST /api/reject now (while regenerations remain, MAX_REGENERATIONS=3 per upload) sets phase 'regenerating' and a worker calls Pipeline.regenerate: ReportAgents runs again on the SAME frame findings and evidence (no vision call, no new quota for the video), and every generator prompt of that run carries the rejected statements and the reviewer's reason (state 'note'). The judge and guardrails are unchanged and judge only against sources. Audit: report:regenerate (actor = rejecting reviewer, resource = rejected report id, detail status/new_report_id/attempts); the rejection itself is stored as before. Result: new draft -> phase pending_review (new report, approval cleared) or the normal failure phase; the page shows a toast from status.notice {id,text} for both outcomes. After the limit a rejection is final (phase rejected). Reset/upload are refused while regenerating. Judged ceiling: the reviewer's reason is free text placed in the generator prompt outside <source> tags (it is the clinician's instruction); outputs still pass the citation check, judge and guardrails. Not seen in a browser.

User chose this on 2026-10-27. Plan was re-approved, T18 resumed through genesis control, gate re-run and the independent-review approval re-recorded on the user's instruction.

decisions.title: T19-T21 design: KB loader, RAG proof in reports, on-page guideline chat (MCP deferred)
decisions.text: User wants proof that RAG works and EU/German guideline content in reports. T19 loads dataset/ into the existing Tiger Cloud chunks table with page/title/language so sources are exact. T20 adds guideline-element retrieval queries and an evaluation set (question -> expected document, hit@5/MRR) run live as proof; statements about documentation elements must be guideline-cited recommendations, never invented patient facts (indication, sedation used etc. are not visible in video). T21 adds a chat on the same page (user said 'MCP or same page'): on-page chat first; an MCP stdio server over the same retrieval is ~50 lines and can follow if asked. KNOWN CEILINGS: BM25 index uses text_config 'english', so German passages are found by vector search only unless a second German index is added; about 4,000 chunks of embedding calls must fit Gemini free-tier limits (batched, resumable); Q&A has no chat history and no medical-advice mode (answers only quote what guidelines say). Q&A is a new capability beyond SPEC FR-1..14; it is tied to FR-4/NFR-3 rather than adding a requirement; user may want SPEC amended.

decisions.title: T19: KB loader design and quota handling
decisions.text: python -m surgidoc.kb load|status. PDFs are recognised by content (extension-less S2k short version, ':Zone.Identifier' sidecars skipped), text is read per page so each chunk stores page, document title (text of page 1 before 'Authors'/'Autoren', running headers removed) and language (stopword count). Cleaning: repeated header/footer lines (>=40% of pages in docs of 5+ pages) and bare page numbers dropped, hyphenated line breaks joined, bibliography-looking chunks (>=3 citation/doi hints) dropped (ponytail: no section parsing). Chunks 1,400 chars. PgStore gains title/page/lang (ALTER ... IF NOT EXISTS) plus ids_for/delete_source/counts. Loading is idempotent and resumable (existing chunk ids skipped, one commit per batch of 64), throttled to 24k estimated tokens/minute, a 429 is waited out twice (65 s) and then ends the run cleanly (QuotaReached) with progress saved; smallest documents first. --replace is needed after changing chunking because chunk ids are source#index. Dry run: 2,429 chunks from 14 PDFs (DE long version 1,037; DE short 119; sedation 2026 430). Free-tier embedding limits (100 RPM, 30k TPM, 1k RPD) are community-reported, NOT verified; if RPD is 1,000 the full load takes about 3 days. Finding: before this task the chunks table was EMPTY (0 rows), so no report could ever cite a guideline. KNOWN GAP for T20: cache.memoize in surgidoc/cache.py stores only [text, source, index], so cached retrieval drops page/title; cache.py is outside T19/T20 scope and needs a scope widening.

decisions.title: T20 scope widened to surgidoc/cache.py (user-approved)
decisions.text: cached_retrieve stores only [text, source, index], so cache hits lose page/title/lang that T19 added; fixing it needs surgidoc/cache.py. Scope hand-edited into project.json, plan re-approved, T20 resumed through genesis control. T19 completed with 962 of 2,429 chunks loaded (embedding quota); remaining loads are reruns of python -m surgidoc.kb load dataset.

decisions.title: T20: RAG proof, guideline reminders in reports, keyword fallback
decisions.text: (1) ReportAgents asks the findings question (4 passages) plus four fixed report-element questions (STAR report elements, informed consent, sedation monitoring/documentation, German Dokumentation/Qualitaetsanforderungen; 2 passages each), duplicates dropped, ~10 passages; a failing element question is skipped, a failing findings question still raises. (2) The generator is told to write video statements first and then up to four guideline reminders citing only K ids, never patient-specific facts not in a source; sources are given to model with document title and page. Reminders (statements whose sources are all K) are shown as 'Guideline reminder' in the UI and under 'Guideline reminders for this report' in the PDF; guideline sources show 'title, p. N'. (3) cache.py stores page/title/lang (version v2). (4) search_with_fallback: on HTTP 429 from the embedder, search falls back to BM25+rerank so a report is not lost when the free embedding quota is spent. (5) python -m surgidoc.kb eval [--keyword-only]: 12 questions (11 English, 1 German) with expected documents; hit@5 and MRR; result in data/kb_eval.json (git-ignored). PROOF 2026-10-27 on 962 stored chunks, keyword-only: asked 12, hit@5 1.00, MRR 0.90 (rank 2 for duodenoscope question, rank 3 for EUS sampling). Hybrid run pending until the embedding quota resets. CAVEATS: questions were written by the assistant after seeing the document list and score document-level hits, not passage-level answers, so this shows retrieval finds the right guideline, not that answers are correct. (6) Live end-to-end run on data/demo/demo_video.mp4: 4 video statements + 4 guideline reminders citing STAR p.6/9, informed consent p.2/4, propofol p.1/7 and DE S2k p.31/34, but status blocked_by_guardrails: rule 'sensitive' matched 'documented in the medical record' (pattern 'medical record' in guardrails.py meant for record numbers). User chose to LEAVE the guardrail as is (2026-10-27), so reports with such reminders can be blocked and need a rerun; narrowing the pattern to 'medical record number' is the known fix.

decisions.title: T21: guideline Q&A on the page
decisions.text: surgidoc/qa.py GuidelineQA: retrieve (cached, keyword fallback) -> one 'generator' model call returning JSON {answer, sources, covered} with passages as <passage> data -> citations validated (1..N, ints), renumbered by first appearance in the text; no valid citation or covered=false = 'not covered', nothing retrieved = no model call; answer checked only for the 'injection' guardrail rule (report-only rules for diagnosis/treatment/sensitive do not apply to quoted guideline wording such as doses or 'medical record'). POST /api/ask {name, question}: registered users with permission report:view (all three roles), denials audited, question <=500 chars without control characters, one question at a time (429 otherwise), audit stores only question length and covered flag, never the text; errors are plain and carry no details. Works with no video. Live check 2026-10-27 on the real DB: English consent question cited informed-consent pp.4/9, German documentation question cited S2k pp.31/33/34, off-topic question answered 'not covered'. CEILINGS: no judge pass (reports have one); no chat history; keyword-only retrieval while the embedding quota is spent; MCP server not built (about 50 lines over the same retrieve if wanted).

decisions.title: T22: embedding model switched to gemini-embedding-2; metrics tooling
decisions.text: The free daily quota of gemini-embedding-001 was used up (962 of 2,429 chunks). User asked for a different model: gemini-embedding-2 (Google docs, April 2026: text+image+video+audio+PDF, 768 dims via outputDimensionality, no taskType; task goes in the text: documents 'title: {title} | text: {content}', queries 'task: search result | query: {content}'). Its vector space is NOT compatible with 001, so every chunk is re-embedded. Safety: every row stores embed_model; vector search filters embed_model = current model, ids_for() only counts rows of the current model (old rows are re-embedded by a normal 'kb load', no --replace needed), kb status counts current-model rows, and BM25 still sees old rows. CachedEmbedder keys already include the model. GeminiEmbedder keeps the 001 behaviour when model='gemini-embedding-001'. Live probe: 768 dims, query/passage cosine 0.80. Metrics added: kb eval --compare (bm25, bm25+rerank, vector, hybrid RRF, hybrid+rerank; hit@5, MRR, precision@5, nDCG@5; one query embedding per question), kb eval --abstain (off-topic 'not covered' rate and in-scope answer rate; about 10 model calls), python -m surgidoc.validate (full pipeline on one CholecSeg8k video built into an mp4, 2 s per frame, scored against masks: structure recall, absent mentions, unclear rate, judge approved, guardrails passed, citation validity, guideline reminders, seconds; dev split default, test split needs --final and is logged). Relevance in the retrieval metrics is per document, not per passage. KNOWN FLAKE: tests/test_webui.py::test_uploads_without_a_content_length_are_refused fails about 1 run in 10 (client/server close race after the 411), which also explains the occasional first-run gate failure; not changed.

knowledge.title: Gemini free-tier models and limits
knowledge.text: ai.google.dev pricing (2026-10-26): free of charge input/output for gemini-2.5-flash, 2.5-flash-lite, 3.6-flash, 3.5-flash-lite, 3.1-flash-lite. Per-model RPM/TPM/RPD are NOT published on the rate-limits page (view in AI Studio); limits are per project, RPD resets midnight Pacific, 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on breach. Free tier content may be used to improve products: public data only. Gateway: configurable routes+limits, conservative defaults, 429 is ground truth.

knowledge.title: Kaggle auth verified: KGAT_ value in KAGGLE_KEY works only as an API token

knowledge.title: cholecseg8k structure, class table and download constraints (verified from Kaggle API)
knowledge.text: 17 videos (video01, 09, 12, 17, 18, 20, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 35, 37, 43, 48, 52, 55); 101 clip dirs of 80 frames named videoNN/videoNN_START/frame_IDX_endo.png + _endo_color_mask.png + _endo_mask.png + _endo_watershed_mask.png. Per frame: endo ~400 KB, watershed mask ~6 KB. Watershed pixel value = class id hex (dataset description Table I): 0 Black Background 0x50, 1 Abdominal Wall 0x11, 2 Liver 0x21, 3 Gastrointestinal Tract 0x13, 4 Fat 0x12, 5 Grasper 0x31, 6 Connective Tissue 0x23, 7 Blood 0x24, 8 Cystic Duct 0x25, 9 L-hook Electrocautery 0x32, 10 Gallbladder 0x22, 11 Hepatic Vein 0x33, 12 Liver Ligament 0x05. Not every class appears in every frame. Download constraints: ~1 MB/s (full 2.89 GB archive ~48 min) and the WSL VM restarted uncleanly (EXT4 recovery) mid-download, killing it at 62 MB: use a resumable file-by-file subset downloader in foreground tool calls, never one long background job. Evaluation split must be BY VIDEO (frames within a video are near-duplicates): proposed 3 dev videos (tuning allowed), 3 held-out test videos (final reporting only, runs logged), rest unused for now.

knowledge.title: CORRECTION: cholecseg8k watershed pixel values are DECIMAL class numbers
knowledge.text: Verified on a real mask (video01_00080/frame_80): values 21 (liver 51%), 50 (background 17%), 22 (gallbladder 17%), 12 (fat 7%), 13 (GI tract 6.5%) and 255 (0.6% boundary pixels, ignored). So: 50 Background, 11 Abdominal Wall, 21 Liver, 13 Gastrointestinal Tract, 12 Fat, 31 Grasper, 23 Connective Tissue, 24 Blood, 25 Cystic Duct, 32 L-hook Electrocautery, 22 Gallbladder, 33 Hepatic Vein, 5 Liver Ligament. The earlier record read the description's '#505050' column as hex (0x50) which was WRONG; synthetic unit tests had hidden it, the opt-in live test caught it. Other facts unchanged: 17 videos, 101 clips of 80 frames, ~0.4 MB per frame+mask, ~1 MB/s, split by video, VM restarts mean resumable foreground downloads only.

knowledge.title: First real-frame evaluation (dev split, run 1, Gemini vision only)
knowledge.text: 2026-10-27, 36 dev frames from video09/video20/video55 (CholecSeg8k, cholecystectomy, NOT GI endoscopy), describer = Gemini vision via gateway 'vision' route (gemini-3.6-flash), no EndoViT. mean_recall 0.325 (share of mask-labelled structures the description mentions), absent_mention_rate 0.111 (frames naming a labelled class that is absent from the mask), unclear_rate 0.0 (the safety prompt does NOT cause over-refusal on real frames). Per-class recall: Abdominal Wall 0.00, Fat 0.56, Liver 0.53, Gallbladder 0.42, Grasper 0.42, L-hook Electrocautery 0.17, Liver Ligament 0.17, GI Tract 0.12. CAVEATS: recall is a LOWER BOUND under a crude keyword matcher (e.g. 'electrosurgical device' is not matched to L-hook; 'stomach'/'ligamentous' partial), the prompt never asks for an exhaustive structure list, Abdominal Wall is nearly always labelled but never named, and only the 13 labelled classes can be judged. Test split (video01/video18/video43, 36 frames) is downloaded but untouched: no test_runs.json. Tuning (prompt, synonyms) may use DEV only; one final TEST run at the end. Reproduce: surgidoc.dataset.prepare(...) then evaluate_split(describer, 'data/cholecseg8k', 'dev'); results saved in data/cholecseg8k/dev_eval_run1.json (git-ignored, CC BY-NC-SA).
